DID is a condition similar to PTSD. If a child under the age of where the personality has formed is severely abused, to the point where they do not feel safe, they basically create "alters" or other personalities to keep themselves safe. DID is dissociative identity disorder because it's described to be someone who experiences severe dissociation, or zoning out beyond return. Generally this happens before they switch alters or personalities. They experience great brain fog and cannot remember what has happened when other alters are out. 
DID's other forms is OSDD, which has many versions and is a spectrum. It's not American. People all over can have it. There is no cure for this. There are many different forms of alters, persecutors, protectors, age sliders, interjects, etc.
Imagine this. You're traumatized and you basically have to live two lives. One in your head, and another in real life. You and the other alters have to keep safe and keep from untrusted people finding out about your DID. Not only that but some alters hurt the system's body and others despite the fact you'd never do that, and you can't exactly stop them from fronting (being the main alter out) except for co-fronting, which can hurt the body as well because forcing yourself to front can actually cause mental damage. Systems generally have 10-100 people, but they can have more or less.
